text:
A catheter valve (a flip-flo valve) generally isn't suitable when the patient has poor manual dexterity or cognitive impairment that prevents them from operating it reliably, when they have a small-capacity or overactive bladder with high pressures or reduced bladder compliance, or when they have significant urinary retention/vesicoureteral reflux risk or active urinary tract infection that makes intermittent, non-continuous drainage unsafe. It's also avoided in the immediate post-operative period or whenever continuous drainage is needed (e.g., to monitor output, or with hematuria and clot risk), and in patients who can't sense bladder fullness. This is general information, so the choice should be confirmed with the patient's clinician or continence nurse.

CONFIDENCE: 72
